### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 37 pages)`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1ca8741dda9ff8f72d1a1d3cbef5c0fb3dc687e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0807fd8143b00ae1eebb769e33c59769ee3c1223`

Head verified (PR `head.sha` agrees); two commits over merge-base `44ce049a8c`; 4 files, +10/−3. PR #19892's `en` rewrite (`029d8a4710`) is an ancestor of the merge-base, and neither `sys-user.object.ts` nor `en.objects.generated.ts` changed between it and head, so the `en` translated from is the current one. CI at head, latest per name over 32 names at the last poll: 22 `success`, 3 `skipped`, 7 in progress, 0 failed. `Vercel` is an external commit status. No derived gate re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

(a) Faithful in all three locales. The `en` source (`sys-user.object.ts:704` = `en.objects.generated.ts:38`, byte-identical) makes four claims. C1: a legacy better-auth role scalar (admin, user, …). C2: no longer written (ADR-0068 D2). C3: route 1, a VERIFIED email listed in `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`, on every posture. C4: route 2, an unscoped `admin_full_access` assignment in `sys_user_permission_set`, on the `single` posture only, "also confers".
- zh-CN: C1–C4 ✓. The `single` qualifier sits after the semicolon and governs only the `admin_full_access` clause; 已验证的邮箱 = verified email; 未限定范围 = unscoped.
- ja-JP: C1–C4 ✓. Route 2 is its own sentence opening with `single` テナンシー態勢では, so the qualifier cannot leak onto route 1; 確認済みメールアドレス = verified email.
- es-ES: C1–C4 ✓. The `single` qualifier is after the semicolon; correo verificado; sin ámbito = unscoped. "valor de rol" renders "role scalar" as "role value", which changes no claim.
All four code spans are verbatim in all three locales. No translation extends the `single`-only route to every posture, and none drops "verified".

(b) Each locale file changes exactly one line (the `help` value at line 38). No key, structure or sidecar changes; none of the six hash files carries this leaf (0 hits). The retired action (`Set Platform Role` / 设置平台角色 / プラットフォームロールを設定 / `Establecer rol de plataforma` / `setPlatformRole` / `set_platform_role` / `set-platform-role`) has 0 hits across all 98 non-test files under a `translations/` directory at head, `en` included. At the merge-base the same grep hits exactly the three lines this PR replaces.

(c) The refutation holds on the code. `collectFilledFromHashes` writes a hash only when the value equals the `en` source or the previous record matches its hash; a genuine translation satisfies neither (`source-hash.test.ts:270` pins "records nothing for the leaves that were translated"). A hand entry is forbidden: AGENTS.md's `**/translations/*.generated.ts` row, and the file header says "Do not hand-edit". It would also fail: `extract --check` compares the companion byte-for-byte; an entry of `hash(en)` never fires; an entry of `hash(translation)` would fire forever and make `withSourceFallback` serve English. `Fixes #19897` is right. The card's "What happens" defect is fixed and verified. The hash entry sat under "Suggested shape (⛔ not a ruling)", and the dispatch allowed the sidecar only through the tooling, which wrote nothing.

(d) Every checkable claim in the changeset and PR body is true: the `en` text moved twice (`4215417220` for #17102, `029d8a4710` for #19892); the stale text dates from `033a34c7c4` (#11530); there is no hash entry; the retired-name grep is 0. Two wording nits, neither actionable: the changeset says the `en` text was "renamed" (it was rewritten), and its second paragraph is more process narrative than an upgrader needs, though every sentence is true.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `Clause-②: no`: CORRECT. Three translated help strings change. No key set, accept set, export or authorable surface moves, and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- ③-1 The dev's open question: should genuinely translated `objects` / `metadataForms` leaves get staleness protection? This PR correctly builds nothing. The ~1200-per-locale legacy-trusted population is the ruled status quo, not an oversight. #8765 Option B (5299847077) ruled the hand-recorded hash for the hand-authored sections only. #12069 Option A extended the mechanism to generated bundles as a generator-owned table, and its body and module note name the translated-leaf residue as the design. The dev's option B would be a new ruling, not a reuse. It needs either a second table on one path, which `source-hash.ts` refuses, or an extractor format change, which #12069's intake (5407905029) put on the human floor. Reviewer's recommendation: a `[Decision]` card citing #8765 / #12069 / #9672, with this card as the incident. The seat disposes of it (see the ACCEPT).
- ③-2 1203 / 1182 / 1173 translated `objects` leaves (zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES) carry no hash. Not audited for actual staleness. ACCEPTABLE: triage asked for exactly this measurement and forbade widening the card; it is evidence for ③-1, not a defect of this PR.
- ③-3 No source-hash entry added: ACCEPTABLE, per ①(c).
- ③-4 Precision nit, in the os-dev-report only. `findStaleFills` does walk recorded `objects.*` paths; a hand entry fails for the conjunct reason in ①(c), not a walk reason. ACCEPTABLE: the PR body and changeset do not repeat it.
- ③-5 `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally (exit 3): ACCEPTABLE. The diff is translation content only, and CI's Build Core is green at head.
- ③-6 Do not land until Lint & Repo Gates (the live `check:i18n` / `check:i18n-stale-fill`) and Test Core finish green.
